projects.name: A single window system is established for the facilitation of economic activity in free economic zones in Tajikistan
projects.description:
In a letter dated 25 December 2023, H.E. Mr Zavqizoda Zavqi Amin, Minister of Economic Development and Trade of Tajikistan, requested UNIDO’s technical assistance to support the digital transformation of the national economy. Following consultations with the Ministry, UNIDO explored opportunities for technical assistance to strengthen the national digital innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystems in line with Tajikistan’s strategic priorities for digital economy development.

UNIDO subsequently developed the current project to support the implementation of the National Development Strategy 2030 and the Mid-Term Programme for the Development of the Digital Economy in Tajikistan for 2021 to 2025. The project strengthens the Government’s digital transformation efforts through two main intervention areas. The first focuses on free economic zones, industrial clusters and small and medium-sized enterprises in selected priority sectors. The second supports key public sector initiatives to facilitate technology and knowledge transfer, enhance public sector efficiency, increase small and medium-sized enterprise productivity and international competitiveness and foster a digital and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Through these interventions, the project seeks to facilitate Tajikistan’s integration into the wider Eurasian economic landscape by strengthening linkages and accelerating the transition towards a more digital and innovative economy.

projects.name: Capacity building to improve access to affordable and clean energy for all
projects.description:
- Preparation phase for the project "Improving the energy efficiency of the global building supply chain industry and its products to deliver high performance buildings", Mapping of key stakeholders / project partners, appraisal mission to validate the baseline situations, final validation workshop for full project document. Tajikistan is one of seven beneficiary countries.
- Sustainable hydrogen production in the UNECE region and its role in the development of a hydrogen ecosystem and export potential: Develop recommendations for a coherent international system of standardisation and certification of hydrogen in the context of the Paris agreement and Agenda 2030 implementation
-RPTC project "Supporting electric mobility as enabler of the digital and green transformations in the UNECE region". Tajikistan is one of the beneficiary countries
- RPTC project "Digitalization in support of energy systems’ transformation in the UNECE region". Tajikistan is one of the beneficiary countries.
- Study with assessment of possible alternative uses of coal

In 2026: 
- To strengthen national capacities in the target countries for the development of comprehensive digital governance policies to better plan and manage integrated power systems for an inclusive and gender-responsive sustainable digital transformation of the energy sector. 
The project is grounded in the understanding that many countries with special needs face fragmented governance systems, outdated and/or damaged infrastructure, and limited technical capacity to integrate digital technologies into power systems. Without structured and inclusive policy frameworks, efforts to deploy smart grids and decentralized renewable energy technologies often remain ad hoc, vulnerable to rebound effects, and unable to ensure interoperability with legacy systems. Additionally, the digital divide, cybersecurity risks, and underrepresentation of women and marginalized groups in energy decision-making processes further hinder the inclusiveness and sustainability of the energy transition. 
To address these challenges, the project will support target countries – Belarus, Tajikistan, Egypt, Jordan, Mongolia, and Georgia – to develop national digital governance frameworks tailored to their energy system contexts (OP1.1). These frameworks will be complemented by capacity-building workshops (OP1.2) and the creation of a harmonized policy toolkit (OP1.3), helping policymakers and regulators apply digital governance principles in planning, managing, and regulating smart grid systems. 
In parallel, the project will facilitate increased cross-country cooperation through the establishment of a regional platform for knowledge exchange on digital energy governance (OP2.1). This platform will foster peer learning, mentorship, and the sharing of best practices among national institutions, regional actors, and the private sector. Policy briefs and country case studies (OP2.2) will summarize key insights and inform ongoing reforms, while national training events (OP2.3) will reinforce technical capacity and promote a responsible and inclusive digital transition. 
- Strengthening Sustainable Critical Raw Material Production in Central Asia. The project’s objective is to improve governance, accountability, and sustainability of critical raw material (CRM) supply chains in Central Asia to support socio-economic development and the energy transition.
